processing: Orthodox black tea, in contrast to the CTC that makes up most Nilgiri output; the estate also makes green and handmade teas.
harvest_season: Not specified for this estate; the Nilgiris pick for much of the year, unlike the sharply seasonal gardens of northern India.
appearance_dry: Dark twisted leaf in the whole-leaf grades, and smaller dark particles in BOP.
appearance_wet: Coppery brown leaf, typical of Nilgiri orthodox tea.
taste_profile: Described as brisk and full-bodied with floral undertones and a smooth, refreshing finish.

brewing.notes: Western-style. As with other Nilgiris, it is forgiving and also makes a clean iced tea.

vintage_note: Sold by grade (such as OP and BOP) rather than by a vintage year or named flush, and packed under the estate's own label as well as through tea merchants. Check for a packing date, and drink it within a year or two.
description:
Glendale is a Nilgiri estate near Coonoor in Tamil Nadu, and one of the names that shows a Nilgiri garden can make more than bulk CTC. Its sellers give a range of 1,650 to 2,120 m, in cold, misty hills.

The core of the range is orthodox black tea in grades including OP and BOP. There are also green and handmade teas, plus flavoured blends with mint, tulsi or cardamom, which are a different thing from the single-garden leaf.

Expect a brisk, bright cup with some floral lift, lighter than Assam and rounder than a first flush Darjeeling. Three minutes in water just off the boil is a good start, and it holds up well when iced.

For the garden's character, choose an unflavoured whole-leaf grade. The broken grades suit a stronger breakfast cup, and the blends tell you little about the estate.
history:
Glendale is counted among the historically significant Nilgiri estates, but its age is unclear. One seller traces its roots to the early 1800s, which is hard to square with Coonoor Tea Estate being described as the region's first commercial estate in 1854.

Today it is managed by Glenworth Estate Ltd, which describes three gardens across more than 525 hectares.
